newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-BROADHURST BOOSTS RYDER CUP CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BROADHURST BOOSTS RYDER CUP CHALLENGE.

text.p: Ryder Cup hopeful Paul Broadhurst ended a five-week lean spell by taking the early lead in the European Tournament Players' championship on Thursday.

Britain's Broadhurst had put himself in cup contention with a second place in the Cannes Open last month and a third in the Portuguese Open in March. But the 1991 Ryder debutant at Kiawah Island, where he won both his matches, then lost ground, his poor run coinciding with the birth of his third child.
By this week Broadhurst was still in an automatic 10th qualifying place but needing to recharge his bid.
He did that with five birdies and just one bogey in a four-under-par 68 on a tough day at Gut Kaden where scores soared because of a cold, veering wind.
"I don't want to use the birth as an excuse," said Broadhurst, who headed tournament favourite Bernhard Langer, his playing partner, by three shots.

"I didn't drive the ball well in Cannes even though I was second and I've been trying to find a solution since. On Monday, before the final round of the (British) PGA I found something with my coach I could work on and though I didn't go into this round with much confidence, I gradually got it back.

"I'd been in a very good position for the Ryder Cup but lots of guys have gone mad over the past few weeks and overtaken me. It's very important to me and if I don't get in I'll feel as though I've blown it."
